t: This is the Prescott Channel, part of the Bow Back Rivers in east London. It was built between 1930 and 1935 as a flood relief scheme for the River Lee Navigation, in what was then the County Borough of West Ham. It's named after Sir William Prescott, who was then chairman of the Lee Conservancy Board. He was an engineer and Conservative politician. In 1962, rubble from the demolished Euston Arch was used to improve the channel.
